name: Tennessee

notes: Food and food ingredients are taxed at a reduced 4% state rate plus the local rate (Hendersonville's lower 2.25% local rate on food is used there); candy, dietary supplements and prepared food aren't food and pay the full 7% plus the local rate, which is not counted here.
Alcohol bought in stores: beer, wine and spirits bought in stores are taxed at the full rate (wine in grocery stores included), on top of excise taxes left out here.

Drinks served pay the sales tax plus, on spirits, wine and high-alcohol beer (over 8% alcohol by weight), the 15% liquor-by-the-drink tax on top of it (TCA 57-4-301), counted here on drinks with spirits or wine, 70% of drinks served nationally (2022 Economic Census). Ordinary beer served pays only the sales tax; high-alcohol beer isn't separated.

Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at the full rate, on top of excise taxes left out here: 62 cents a pack of cigarettes, 6.6% of the wholesale price on other tobacco, and 10% of the wholesale price on vapor products since July 1, 2025.
Barber and beauty services aren't taxed.
Clothing is taxed. The yearly sales tax holiday (July 31 to August 2 in 2026) exempted clothing and school supplies of $100 or less an item, which is not taken out here.
Laundry and dry cleaning: laundering and dry cleaning are taxed; coin-operated self-service laundry is not.
Motor fuel is exempt from the sales tax and taxed by the gallon instead: 27.4 cents for gasoline (26 cents plus a 1.4-cent petroleum fee), left out here.
Local tax applies only to the first $1,600 of any single item, and the state adds 2.75% on the part from $1,600 to $3,200; not modeled, which matters little for everyday store sales.
Diapers and menstrual products are taxed at the full rate (2026 bills to exempt them stalled, as reported).
Hotel stays pay city and county hotel taxes (Memphis 4% plus a $2-a-night tourism fee, Shelby County 5%, Pigeon Forge 2.5%, Sevierville 3%), which are not counted here.
gaps: 13 cities lie in more than one county with a different rate in each county part; a tract at least half in such a city takes the rate of its own county part.

Davidson County's 0.5% transit surtax is counted on top of its 2.25% local rate (2.75% in all). Pigeon Forge's and Sevierville's restaurant taxes are counted; other city restaurant and hotel taxes are not. Votes on November 3, 2026 (Goodlettsville; Moore County, reported) and Davidson County's lower food rate from November 1 are noted on those pages.

tiers.label: Tennessee jobs tax credit enhancement tier
tiers.what: All tiers get a $4,500 per-job credit with 25-year carryforward; Tier 2 adds 3 more years at $4,500/yr and Tiers 3-4 add 5 more years. Minimum net new jobs: 25 (Tiers 1-2), 20 (Tier 3), 10 (Tier 4), plus $500,000 capital investment.

programs: Tourism Development Zones are mapped from the Department of Revenue's layer (nine zones); the Comptroller's list also names Memphis Graceland and Memphis Fairgrounds zones, which the layer doesn't draw, and doesn't name the Bristol, Kingsport and East Ridge zones the layer does. A 2026 bill extending Nashville's zone to 2043 passed the state House on April 22, 2026, as reported; whether it became law wasn't confirmed.

Business improvement districts are mapped for Nashville (Metro's tax districts) and Memphis (the Downtown Memphis Commission's Central Business Improvement District, from the City's open data). Chattanooga's Central Business Improvement District (created in 2019 and run by River City Company as the Downtown Chattanooga Alliance) isn't mapped: the City publishes no layer of it, and River City Company's own layer isn't an official City map. Knoxville's has no official map found. Tax increment districts are mapped for Nashville (MDHA's redevelopment districts) and Memphis (the Community Redevelopment Agency's three); Knoxville's and Chattanooga's aren't (no official map found). Tennessee Main Street communities (50, by TNECD's count) have no published boundaries.

warn.text: Nashville draws many visitors, but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy: its seasonal homes (1.1%) and its 495 lodging places (0.7 per 1,000 residents) are spread over a large city, though 15 of its 166 census tracts are flagged on their own. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local, most of all downtown.

Memphis draws many visitors, most of all downtown, but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy: its seasonal homes (0.4%) and its 332 lodging places (0.5 per 1,000 residents) are spread over a large city, though 11 of its 185 census tracts are flagged on their own. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local, most of all downtown.

Chattanooga draws many visitors, but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy: its seasonal homes (0.9%) and its 223 lodging places (1.2 per 1,000 residents) fall under the flag's cutoffs, though 6 of its 49 census tracts are flagged on their own. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.
